tomato_early_blight.sdg_impact: SDG 2.4 - Promotes sustainable food production; avoids up to 35% harvest loss.
tomato_early_blight.symptoms: Concentric rings (target-like spots) on older leaves, lower leaves turning yellow and dropping prematurely.
eco_remedies: Apply copper octanoate or bio-fungicide containing Bacillus subtilis.
Spray neem oil solution (0.5% concentration) bi-weekly as a natural antifungal deterrent.
Prune affected lower leaves immediately and dispose of them away from compost piles.
Apply organic mulch around tomato base to prevent fungal spores from splashing up from soil.
tomato_early_blight.chemical_reduction_advice: Avoid broad-spectrum synthetic chemical fungicides. Relying on bio-fungicides and proper spacing lowers toxic soil runoff by over 80%.
tomato_early_blight.irrigation_and_soil: Switch to drip irrigation. Keep foliage dry, and ensure a minimum 3-year crop rotation.

tomato_healthy.sdg_impact: SDG 2 - Optimal photosynthetic activity, high expected harvest yield.
tomato_healthy.symptoms: Uniform deep green leaf pigmentation, strong turgidity, no chlorosis or necrotic lesions.
eco_remedies: Maintain existing organic compost feeding routine.
Inspect undersides of leaves weekly for early aphid or whitefly presence.
Apply bio-stimulants such as seaweed extract to reinforce natural plant immunity.
tomato_healthy.chemical_reduction_advice: Zero synthetic chemicals needed. Continue organic biological pest management.
tomato_healthy.irrigation_and_soil: Maintain consistent soil moisture (1-2 inches per week) to prevent blossom-end rot.

potato_late_blight.sdg_impact: SDG 2.4 & SDG 12.3 - Mitigates catastrophic tuber loss and post-harvest decay.
potato_late_blight.symptoms: Dark, water-soaked irregular patches on leaves with white fuzzy fungal growth on leaf undersides under humid conditions.
eco_remedies: Immediately rogue and bury/destroy heavily infected plants to protect adjacent rows.
Apply copper sulfate (Bordeaux mixture) approved for organic farming under high humidity alerts.
Spray horsetail tea extract (Equisetum arvense) rich in natural silica to fortify leaf cuticle cell walls.
potato_late_blight.chemical_reduction_advice: Proactive canopy airflow management reduces reliance on synthetic systemic fungicides by 65%.
potato_late_blight.irrigation_and_soil: Avoid late evening sprinkler irrigation. Hill soil well over tubers to prevent spore wash-down.

corn_common_rust.sdg_impact: SDG 2 - Protects staple grain yields vital for food security in vulnerable regions.
corn_common_rust.symptoms: Oval to elongated cinnamon-brown pustules on upper and lower leaf surfaces.
eco_remedies: Introduce beneficial microorganisms (e.g., Trichoderma harzianum soil and foliar treatments).
Dust with micro-fine wettable sulfur early in disease onset if humidity remains above 80%.
Adopt rust-resistant hybrid seed varieties for subsequent planting cycles.
corn_common_rust.chemical_reduction_advice: Encouraging natural hyperparasites naturally curtails rust spread without pesticide resistance.
corn_common_rust.irrigation_and_soil: Ensure balanced nitrogen application; excessive synthetic nitrogen stimulates lush, susceptible vegetative growth.

bell_pepper_bacterial_spot.sdg_impact: SDG 12 & SDG 13 - Prevents defoliation and sunscald without heavy synthetic chemicals.
bell_pepper_bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, yellow-green spots turning brown with greasy margins; causes premature leaf drop and fruit lesions.
eco_remedies: Apply bactericides formulated with fixed copper combined with Bacillus amyloliquefaciens.
Spray garlic and ginger aqueous extracts shown to inhibit bacterial motility.
Strictly sanitize pruning shears with 70% alcohol between handling each plant row.
bell_pepper_bacterial_spot.chemical_reduction_advice: Utilize certified pathogen-free hot-water-treated seeds rather than prophylactic antibiotic sprays.
bell_pepper_bacterial_spot.irrigation_and_soil: Never work among wet plants. Increase plant spacing to 45cm to promote rapid drying.
